name: Andhra Pradesh
intro: A long-coastline state of ancient Buddhist sites, the hill temple of Tirupati, spicy cuisine and the dramatic Gandikota gorge.
culture: Andhra blends Telugu literary tradition, Kuchipudi dance and a strong temple culture with a famously fiery cuisine.
travel_tips: Book Tirupati darshan slots in advance.
Carry sun protection along the coast.

name: Arunachal Pradesh
intro: India's easternmost state of high passes, Buddhist monasteries, dense forests and dozens of distinct tribal cultures.
best_time_to_visit: March to October; permits required for all visitors.
culture: A mosaic of more than 25 major tribes, from the Monpa of Tawang to the Apatani of Ziro, each with unique festivals and crafts.
travel_tips: Indian citizens need an Inner Line Permit; foreigners need a Protected Area Permit.
Roads are slow—plan generous travel time.

name: Assam
intro: The gateway to the Northeast, land of the mighty Brahmaputra, one-horned rhinos, tea gardens and the river island of Majuli.
culture: Assam's culture centres on the Brahmaputra, Vaishnavite satras, Bihu dance and a globally famous tea heritage.
travel_tips: Kaziranga safaris run mid-winter to spring.
Book Majuli ferries with buffer time.

name: Bihar
intro: A cradle of ancient India, home to Bodh Gaya where the Buddha attained enlightenment and the ruins of Nalanda university.
culture: Bihar carries deep Buddhist, Jain and Hindu heritage, Madhubani painting and the grand Chhath festival.
travel_tips: Bodh Gaya is busiest in winter pilgrimage season.
Combine Nalanda, Rajgir and Bodh Gaya on one circuit.

name: Chhattisgarh
intro: A green, tribal heartland of powerful waterfalls, deep forests, ancient temples and the caves of Bastar.
culture: Rich in Adivasi (tribal) traditions, folk dance, bell-metal Dhokra craft and forest-based living.
travel_tips: Chitrakote Falls is most dramatic just after the monsoon.
Bastar's interior is best visited with local guides.

name: Goa
intro: India's smallest state by area, a sun-soaked blend of beaches, Portuguese heritage, Konkani culture and a laid-back susegad spirit.
culture: A unique Indo-Portuguese fusion visible in the architecture, cuisine, music, carnival and churches.
travel_tips: Prices peak sharply around Christmas and New Year.
Rent a scooter to explore hidden beaches.

name: Gujarat
intro: The vibrant western state of the white Rann of Kutch, Asiatic lions at Gir, Gandhi's legacy and dazzling Navratri nights.
best_time_to_visit: October to March; the Rann Utsav runs through winter.
culture: Gujarat combines a strong trading tradition, colourful textiles, vegetarian cuisine and the world's longest dance festival, Navratri.
travel_tips: Gir safaris need advance permits.
The white Rann is best under a full moon.

name: Haryana
intro: A largely agrarian state wrapped around Delhi, home to the battlefield of Kurukshetra and lively highway-town culture.
culture: Haryana is known for its robust rural traditions, folk dance, wrestling akharas and the Gita heritage of Kurukshetra.
travel_tips: Surajkund Mela is a highlight for crafts lovers.
Sultanpur is best in winter for migratory birds.

name: Himachal Pradesh
intro: A Himalayan playground of hill stations, apple orchards, high-altitude Spiti and Kinnaur, and countless trekking trails.
best_time_to_visit: March to June and September to November; Spiti in summer.
culture: From the colonial charm of Shimla to the Buddhist Trans-Himalaya of Spiti, Himachal spans lush valleys and cold deserts.
travel_tips: Spiti's high passes open only in summer.
Carry warm layers year-round in the higher valleys.

name: Jharkhand
intro: A forested plateau state of waterfalls, tribal heritage, the sacred Parasnath hill and rich mineral belts.
culture: Home to numerous Adivasi communities, Jharkhand is known for Sohrai and Kohbar wall art and forest-based traditions.
travel_tips: Waterfalls near Ranchi peak after the monsoon.
Parasnath is a major Jain pilgrimage climb.

name: Karnataka
intro: A diverse southern state spanning the ruins of Hampi, the palaces of Mysore, Coorg's coffee hills and a quiet Konkan coast.
culture: Karnataka pairs a glorious temple-building heritage (Chalukya, Hoysala, Vijayanagara) with a modern tech capital in Bengaluru.
travel_tips: Coorg and the Western Ghats are lush right after the monsoon.
Hampi needs at least two full days.

name: Kerala
intro: 'God's Own Country', a lush ribbon of backwaters, tea-clad hills, Ayurveda, spice gardens and vibrant Kathakali art.
culture: Kerala's culture spans temple festivals, Kathakali and Theyyam, martial art Kalaripayattu and a strong Ayurvedic tradition.
travel_tips: Book Alleppey houseboats in advance in peak season.
Onam is the best time to experience Kerala culture.

name: Madhya Pradesh
intro: The 'Heart of India', home to the temples of Khajuraho, tiger reserves, the marble rocks of Bhedaghat and Bundela Orchha.
culture: Madhya Pradesh holds superb temple and fort heritage, tribal art, and some of India's finest tiger habitat.
travel_tips: Bandhavgarh offers among the best tiger-sighting odds.
Khajuraho's Western Group is unmissable.

name: Maharashtra
intro: A powerhouse state of the Ajanta and Ellora caves, Sahyadri forts, hill stations and the metropolis of Mumbai.
best_time_to_visit: October to March; the Sahyadris are magical in the monsoon.
culture: Maharashtra blends Maratha history, Warli tribal art, Ganesh festival fervour and a leading film and business culture.
travel_tips: Ajanta is closed on Mondays, Ellora on Tuesdays.
Sahyadri forts are lush and slippery in the monsoon.

name: Manipur
intro: A 'jewelled land' of the floating Loktak Lake, classical Manipuri dance and the world's only floating national park.
culture: Manipur is the birthplace of the graceful Manipuri classical dance and Polo, with rich Meitei and hill-tribe traditions.
travel_tips: Loktak's phumdis (floating islands) are the highlight.
Check local advisories before travelling.

name: Meghalaya
intro: The 'abode of clouds', a land of living root bridges, thundering waterfalls, crystal rivers and matrilineal Khasi culture.
best_time_to_visit: October to April; the monsoon is spectacular but very wet.
culture: Meghalaya's Khasi, Jaintia and Garo peoples maintain matrilineal societies and remarkable bioengineering of root bridges.
religious_destinations: Cathedral of Mary Help of Christians
travel_tips: The Double Decker root bridge is a strenuous full-day trek.
Umngot river at Dawki is clearest in winter.

name: Mizoram
intro: A serene state of rolling blue hills, bamboo forests, tidy villages and the warm, musical Mizo community.
culture: Mizoram's close-knit, largely Christian society is known for community harmony, bamboo dance and choral singing.
travel_tips: Chapchar Kut is the best time to see the famous bamboo dance.
Reisiek and Phawngpui offer fine trekking.

name: Nagaland
intro: A vibrant hill state of proud Naga tribes, the grand Hornbill Festival and the flower-filled Dzukou Valley.
best_time_to_visit: October to May; the Hornbill Festival is in early December.
culture: Nagaland's 16+ major tribes maintain distinct dress, music, headhunting-era history and warrior traditions.
travel_tips: The Hornbill Festival at Kisama is the cultural highlight of the year.
An Inner Line Permit is required.

name: Odisha
intro: A coastal state of the Jagannath temple at Puri, the Sun Temple of Konark, Chilika lagoon and Odissi classical dance.
culture: Odisha is renowned for the Kalinga school of temple architecture, Odissi dance, Pattachitra painting and appliqué craft.
travel_tips: Puri Rath Yatra draws enormous crowds—plan ahead.
Chilika is best in winter for migratory birds and dolphins.

name: Punjab
intro: The land of the Golden Temple, five rivers, golden wheat fields, exuberant Bhangra and legendary hospitality.
culture: Punjab pulses with Sikh heritage, Bhangra and Gidda dance, langar culture and a hearty, generous spirit.
famous_food: Sarson da Saag with Makki di Roti
travel_tips: Witness the Wagah border ceremony near Amritsar.
The Golden Temple langar serves thousands daily.

name: Rajasthan
intro: The royal desert state of mighty forts, lake palaces, colourful bazaars, camel safaris and living Rajput traditions.
culture: Rajasthan is a treasury of forts and palaces, folk music, puppetry, miniature painting and desert life.
travel_tips: Book Ranthambore safaris well in advance.
Summers are extremely hot—travel in winter.

name: Sikkim
intro: A tiny Himalayan state watched over by Kanchenjunga, dotted with monasteries, alpine lakes and India's first fully organic farms.
best_time_to_visit: March to May and October to November.
culture: Sikkim blends Nepali, Bhutia and Lepcha cultures with Tibetan Buddhism and a pioneering organic, eco-conscious identity.
travel_tips: Permits are needed for Tsomgo, Nathula and North Sikkim.
Sikkim is largely plastic-restricted—carry a reusable bottle.
hero_credit: Original: Yoghya Derivative work: UnpetitproleX · CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Tamil Nadu
intro: A southern heartland of towering temple gopurams, Chola bronzes, hill stations, Bharatanatyam and a rich Tamil literary tradition.
culture: Tamil Nadu preserves one of the world's oldest living languages, magnificent Dravidian temples and classical music and dance.
travel_tips: The temple towns of the Kaveri delta are unmissable.
Ooty and Kodaikanal offer a cool escape.

name: Telangana
intro: A Deccan state of the Charminar and Golconda, the grand Kakatiya temples of Warangal and a distinctive Hyderabadi culture.
culture: Telangana blends Qutb Shahi and Nizami heritage with Deccan temple traditions and the famous Bathukamma flower festival.
travel_tips: Hyderabad's old city is best explored on foot.
Ramoji Film City is a full-day outing.

name: Tripura
intro: A small northeastern state of royal palaces, rock-cut carvings at Unakoti and the lakeside Neermahal water palace.
culture: Tripura blends Bengali and indigenous Tripuri traditions, with a strong legacy of the Manikya royal dynasty.
travel_tips: Unakoti's giant rock reliefs are unique in India.
Neermahal is beautifully lit in the evening.

name: Uttar Pradesh
intro: India's most populous state, holding the Taj Mahal, the sacred ghats of Varanasi and the spiritual heart of the Ganga plains.
culture: Uttar Pradesh is a crossroads of Mughal, Awadhi and Hindu traditions, from Lucknow's tehzeeb to Varanasi's rituals.
travel_tips: See the Taj at sunrise; it is closed on Fridays.
Take a dawn boat ride on the Varanasi ghats.
hero_credit: Yann ; edited by Jim Carter · CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Uttarakhand
intro: 'Devbhumi', the land of the gods, home of the Char Dham pilgrimage, yoga in Rishikesh, alpine meadows and tiger-rich Corbett.
best_time_to_visit: March to June and September to November; Char Dham in summer.
culture: Uttarakhand fuses Himalayan pilgrimage traditions with Garhwali and Kumaoni folk culture and a deep spiritual identity.
travel_tips: Char Dham needs registration and good acclimatisation.
The Valley of Flowers blooms July–August.

name: West Bengal
intro: From the Darjeeling hills and toy train to the Sundarbans mangroves and cultural capital Kolkata, a state of remarkable range.
culture: West Bengal is a heartland of literature, art, cinema, sweets and the all-embracing Durga Puja festival.
travel_tips: Durga Puja transforms Kolkata—book stays early.
The Darjeeling toy train is a UNESCO heritage ride.

name: Andaman & Nicobar Islands
intro: A remote archipelago of turquoise seas, coral reefs, world-class diving and the poignant colonial history of the Cellular Jail.
culture: A cosmopolitan settler mix alongside protected indigenous communities, with a strong maritime and colonial-history layer.
religious_destinations: Local temples and churches in Port Blair
travel_tips: Radhanagar Beach on Havelock is world-famous.
Some islands need permits; Nicobar is largely off-limits.

name: Chandigarh
intro: India's first planned city, designed by Le Corbusier, known for its ordered greenery, the Rock Garden and Sukhna Lake.
culture: A modernist showcase of urban planning, with a relaxed, well-ordered lifestyle and vibrant food and cafe scene.
travel_tips: The Rock Garden of Nek Chand is a must-see.
Sectors make navigation easy and logical.

name: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu
intro: A former Portuguese pocket of quiet beaches, sea forts and colonial churches along the western coast.
culture: A relaxed coastal blend of Gujarati and Portuguese influences, with tribal heritage in the Dadra & Nagar Haveli hills.
travel_tips: Diu Fort and Nagoa Beach are the highlights.
It makes an easy add-on from Gujarat.
hero_credit: Sharada Prasad CS from Berkeley, India · CC BY 2.0

name: Delhi (NCT)
intro: India's capital, a layered city of Mughal monuments, colonial avenues, bustling bazaars and world-class food.
culture: Delhi layers Sultanate, Mughal, colonial and modern India into one dense, cosmopolitan metropolis.
travel_tips: The Metro is the easiest way to get around.
Old Delhi is best explored on a food walk.

name: Jammu & Kashmir
intro: The fabled 'paradise on earth' of Dal Lake shikaras, Mughal gardens, alpine meadows and the Vaishno Devi pilgrimage.
best_time_to_visit: March to October; winter for snow at Gulmarg.
culture: A blend of Kashmiri, Dogra and Pahari cultures, famed for handicrafts, Sufi traditions and Wazwan cuisine.
travel_tips: The Srinagar Tulip Garden blooms briefly in spring.
Check current travel advisories before planning.

name: Ladakh
intro: A high-altitude cold desert of Buddhist monasteries, the blue Pangong Lake, dramatic passes and the Nubra valley.
culture: Ladakh's Tibetan Buddhist culture shapes its monasteries, festivals, prayer flags and mountain-desert way of life.
travel_tips: Spend a day or two acclimatising in Leh.
Many areas need Inner Line Permits.

name: Lakshadweep
intro: India's smallest union territory, a scatter of coral atolls with lagoons, pristine reefs and superb water sports.
culture: An island culture with strong Malayali and maritime roots and a delicate coral-reef ecology.
travel_tips: Entry requires a permit; access is via Kochi.
Agatti and Bangaram are the main visitor islands.

name: Puducherry
intro: A former French colony of mustard-yellow villas, seaside promenades, the Sri Aurobindo Ashram and the utopian township of Auroville.
culture: Puducherry fuses Tamil and French cultures in its cuisine, architecture and a strong spiritual-community presence.
travel_tips: The French Quarter is best explored on foot or by cycle.
Visit Auroville's Matrimandir with a prior booking.
